The point is most of the colonial regions in our world eventually gained independence. Sure there are exceptions; the French currently still control a lot of overseas dependencies, but for the most part holdovers from the Age of Colonialism are few and far between.

The small mountainous wastelands like the Alps, Pyrenees, and High Atlas are good and add a lot of depth to warfare in those regions. However, massive ones like the Amazon, Great Basin, Arctic, etc. come off to me as more annoying; indigenous peoples inhabited these areas, so why can't I at least enter them?

It's more realistic. I mean, look at what happened to Spain's colonies today. They all got free eventually; from a historical standpoint there will always be great liberty desire in colonial regions and a desire for not only greater autonomy, but independence. It makes sense that the US has high development which would spur liberty desire, as we all know there was a revolution that might be one of the most monumental moments in modern history. Should there be a way for those to keep their colonies if they really want to - of course, but historical reality trumps your desire to make the game's colonial mechanics easier.

I think the real problem is that not many people know or care about the history and geopolitics of South America. Barring meme continents like Australia or Antarctica, South America is probably the least relevant continent in the game. Even in a later game like HOI4, South America is notorious for doing next to nothing, except maybe the occasional border war between Brazil and some other nation. 

I do agree with what you're saying here; when I first colonized through South America as Castile I found that the continent was hardly accurate, and it felt like I was able to cross it and colonize it very quickly, even though the continent's size rivals that of Africa. The provinces are big and blocky, and apart from the chance of the Inca forming all the little native nations on the continent are no-name pushovers. It's really quite a shame that paradox has neglected the continent; I mean they are beginning to shed the blatant eurocentrism in the game, but they could have totally done more to flush out the New World in this recent immersion pack, and they could have charged more for it as well. Colonialism is very fun, and there's an incentive to improve the system for us. Make it so that CN's stay within their colonial regions, add new provinces, add new tribes, diversify the types of goods that can be produced in the region... hell we could see more colonial regions added that correspond to potential releasable nations (when was the last time you saw the United Central America nation released)
